_source: Company Man long video, watched in the built-in browser 2026-11-19: frames 0-91 s every 2-5 s, 0.5 s bursts at 50-52 s (chart) and 80.6-81.6 s (chapter card), spot samples 100-745 s (some landed on mid-roll ads and were dropped), word timings from YouTube's transcript panel (2,261 words, ~187 a minute), sound probe 17-81 s. Our own descriptions; shots after 91 s are spot samples. 627K views in 2 months. Opens and closes on a sponsor read (0-17 s, 675-740 s).

hook.firstFrame: sponsor's logo on an orange card (sponsor read runs 0-17 s; the story's hook starts at 24 s)
hook.firstLine: After the sponsor: the two drinks are about the most direct rivalry there is.

shots.picture: sponsor read: logo card, teal-tinted hacker stock footage, URL and QR code card
channel ident: black silhouette man on a white gradient, brand logos pop in around him, serif channel name
split screen: orange half with brand A's bottle and wordmark slides in, blue half with brand B's
split screen crossfades to a VS composite over product photos
macro stock shot of a cold soda can with the parent company's script logo
1990s TV ad clip of the bottle, 4:3 pillarboxed on a flat blue frame
stock footage: a hand holding the bottle, an athlete drinking against the sun
plain bar chart of US market share, blue bars on a dark grey panel inside a blue frame; shown finished
the narrator's black silhouette walks in front of the chart, then brand panels behind him
stock footage of a hand choosing a bottle in a vending machine
chapter card: huge white bold '1960s' on black, product photo cropped on the right
black-and-white archive photo of a scientist in a lab, stock sweat close-ups, a handshake
vintage TV ad clips pillarboxed on blue, chapter card '1970s'
a newspaper headline screenshot on a blue frame with a source line, then retro product ads
bar chart of sales before and after the takeover; old ads of rival drinks
a spokesperson's quote as white bold text on blue, with the name under it
1990s comparison ad graphics, TV ad clips, athletes in ads
market-share bar chart for 2000, chapter cards, ad clips with a basketball star
product beauty shots (bottles on ice), new-label ads, stock footage; spoken questions to the viewer
sponsor read with stock footage and benefit figures
end card: the silhouette on a white-to-navy gradient with the channel name and handle

lines.gist: sponsor read with a discount code
the giant built a near-copy to beat the leader and never got close
a multi-billion market where the leader holds about four times the rival's share
one-sided but eventful, so the story goes decade by decade
the drink was invented at a university for its football team, then bought by a food firm
a quiet decade and the giant's first half-hearted attempt
a bigger owner buys it and turns it into a national habit
everyone piles in during the 1990s; the rival launches and fails to dent the leader
a mega-merger hands the leader to the other cola giant; flavour wars follow
a third brand rises and is bought by the rival's owner
summary, then three questions for the comments
second sponsor read with coverage figures

ending.cta: asks viewers to comment their views and predictions, then a sponsor read and thanks
ending.lastFrame: silhouette end card with the channel name

whyItWorks: The hook states a lopsided rivalry and backs it with one plain market-share chart inside the first minute.
Decade chapter cards (huge white year on black) give a simple map of a 12-minute story.
Real period TV ads, pillarboxed on a flat brand-coloured frame, carry most of the picture and prove each era.
Low production cost: static charts, stock footage and archive clips cut every 3-5 s under a fast, steady voice.
